thread:
oliver (customer): hey folks — running our on-prem k8s installer behind corp firewall. Installer fails at 'fetching model shards' step. Can you share the minimal hosts/ports we need to open? We can't open wide internet access for compliance.
maria (support): sure. can you paste the installer log snippets and confirm if your network does TLS interception (corp proxy doing MITM) or if egress goes through a NAT with DNS split-horizon?
oliver (customer): log excerpt below — saw both cert verify errors and connection refused. we don't have TLS inspect normally but some teams route through a proxy for outbound urls.
```
2026-02-10T12:33:21Z installer: fetching https://registry.redwood.inference/v1/models/xyz/shard-1
2026-02-10T12:33:21Z fetch error: Get "https://registry.redwood.inference/v1/models/xyz/shard-1": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-02-10T12:33:22Z curl: (7) Failed to connect to registry.redwood.inference port 443: Connection refused
2026-02-10T12:33:45Z apt-get update: Temporary failure resolving 'deb.debian.org'
```
kevin (eng-infra): quick qs — is your cluster using an internal DNS resolver that rewrites external names? if so, split-horizon can break SNI-based routing. can you run these from one of the installer pods/nodes: `dig registry.redwood.inference +short` and `curl -v https://registry.redwood.inference/health` (or `openssl s_client -servername registry.redwood.inference -connect registry.redwood.inference:443`) ?
maria (support): to unblock installs we usually recommend permitting the following FQDNs (SNI allowlist) + 443 (and 80 for package mirrors). Minimal hosts to allow (most customers):
- registry.redwood.inference
- models-cdn.redwood-inference.com
- auth.redwood.inference
- telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- deb.debian.org
- security.ubuntu.com
- packages.redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com
- ocsp.digicert.com
- crl3.digicert.com
Ports: TCP 443 (HTTPS), TCP 80 (HTTP for some apt mirrors). Important: allow outbound DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to your resolver or to public DNS if used.
Also: allow SNI passthrough or disable TLS intercept for the redwood domains — TLS MITM will cause x509 verification failures (the installer verifies cert chains).
sara (security): adding that OCSP/CRL endpoints are often overlooked — if your firewall or proxy blocks OCSP responses you'll get certificate verify errors. we strongly prefer SNI-based host allowlist vs IP lists (CDNs change addresses). if your policy requires IPs, we can provide current ranges but they may change.
deploy-bot: internal KB: https://redwood-internal.kb/egress/onprem-install-quicklist — has curl/tests and a one-liner to validate SNI passthrough.
oliver (customer): ran dig and curl from the installer pod: `dig` returns our proxy IP, `curl -v` shows the proxy's cert (corporate MITM) which explains x509. our security team can't turn off inspect for everything; can we whitelist by IP for just those hosts instead?
kevin (eng-infra): you can, but it's brittle. if you must, include OCSP hosts and current CDN IPs. better options:
- configure the proxy to bypass inspection for the redwood FQDNs (recommended)
- configure your pip/apt clients to use your internal artifactory that proxies pypi and apt (then only artifactory needs egress)
Example quick tests we ask you to run from a node:
- `openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood.inference:443 -servername registry.redwood.inference` (should present a Redwood cert chain)
- `curl -I --resolve registry.redwood.inference:443:<ip> https://registry.redwood.inference/health` (force resolution if needed)
maria (support): if you want the exact current CDN endpoints we host models on, tell me and i'll paste the list; but again these are subject to change: we prefer SNI hostnames + OCSP allow.
oliver (customer): we pushed a bypass rule for the FQDNs (SNI passthrough) and added ocsp.digicert.com. installer progressed further but then pip failed with 403 from our proxy when fetching files.pythonhosted.org.
kevin (eng-infra): that 403 is common when the proxy enforces user-agent or blocks unknown endpoints. two options:
1) let packages flow to pypi by allowing files.pythonhosted.org and pypi.org through the proxy bypass
2) point pip to your internal artifactory (pip.conf example):
```
[global]
index-url = https://artifactory.company.local/api/pypi/pypi/simple
trusted-host = artifactory.company.local
```
oliver (customer): option 1 was approved. we allowed files.pythonhosted.org and pypi.org in bypass and re-ran. installer now completed: model shards downloaded and service started. thanks!
maria (support): great — glad it worked. tl;dr we recommend: allow SNI passthrough for registry.redwood.inference + models CDN, allow pypi/files.pythonhosted.org and apt mirrors (deb.debian.org, security.ubuntu.com), and allow OCSP/CRL endpoints (`ocsp.digicert.com`, `crl3.digicert.com`). if you need IPs we can provide a snapshot but prefer hostname/SNI-based rules.
sara (security): note for auditors — document the bypass rules and scope them to the installer CIDR only. happy to review the change record.
oliver (customer): confirmed installer finished after adding SNI passthrough and allowing OCSP — thanks everyone :tada:
